title: Delta-rule associative memory
purpose: Store key-value pairs in a matrix with the error-correcting update M <- M + rate (v - M k) k^T, retrieve with M k, and compare with the Hebbian rule and the minimum-norm memory. Use it to test fast-weight or linear-attention memories for interference and capacity.

entry_points.name: delta_update
entry_points.arguments: memory: value_size by key_size matrix; key; value; rate > 0; normalize_by_key_norm: bool

entry_points.name: store_pairs
entry_points.arguments: keys: rows; values: rows; rate; sweeps (1 to 100000); rule: delta or hebbian; normalize_by_key_norm

entry_points.name: least_squares_memory
entry_points.returns: the minimum-norm memory V (K^T K)^-1 K^T

assumptions: Keys and values are real vectors of fixed length; the memory starts at zero in store_pairs.
Exact one-shot storage needs rate * ||k||^2 = 1; stability needs 0 < rate * ||k||^2 < 2.
guarantees: After a delta update with rate * ||k||^2 = 1, retrieving k returns v exactly (up to rounding).
Writes with keys orthogonal to k leave the retrieval of k unchanged.
With unit keys and rate 1, sweeps from zero converge to least_squares_memory when the keys are independent; divergence raises ValueError.

known_wrong.name: latest_pair_has_no_crosstalk
known_wrong.why: The Hebbian sum v1 k1^T + v2 k2^T retrieves 0.6 for k2 because k1 and k2 overlap; the delta rule removes that crosstalk for the latest pair.

limits: Dense matrices for small key and value sizes (tens to a few hundred). Sweeps converge slowly when keys are nearly parallel. With more pairs than key dimensions the pairs cannot all be stored; sweeps then cycle instead of converging, and least_squares_memory refuses dependent keys. No forgetting, gating or decay terms are modelled.
technique_references: Linear transformers are secretly fast weight programmers (Schlag, Irie and Schmidhuber)
